item.title: AngloGold plans $900 million mine expansion amid stronger profit
item.description: The investment comes as the gold miner aims to incrementally increase production by the end of the decade.
item.dc:creator: Marina Meireles
item.content:encoded:
AngloGold plans $900 million mine expansion amid stronger profit

Marina Meireles | November 5, 2026 | 9:55 am Top Companies   Africa   Latin America   Gold

Geita open pit mine, located in northwestern Tanzania, is AngloGold’s largest single gold mining operation. ( Image: AngloGold Ashanti )

AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE: AU) plans to invest up to $900 million in expanding brownfield operations across its portfolio, targeting a production increase of 300,000 ounces to 450,000 ounces by 2030.

The investments will focus on the Geita gold mine in Tanzania, Siguiri in Guinea and Cuiabá in Brazil, as well as the ongoing ramp-up at Obuasi in Ghana. The company expects the projects to generate real internal rates of return exceeding 35%, Reuters reported.

“These are high-return, capital efficient projects at our operating mines that are expected to provide high-margin ounces and unlock further value from our portfolio,” AngloGold Ashanti CEO Alberto Calderon said in a statement.

The plan is to use existing infrastructure and operational footprints to reduce risk and optimize capital intensity.

Geita will receive the larger portion of the funding, up to $580 million to raise output to 600,000 ounces by 2030. Cuiabá’s expansion will cost between $200 million and $250 million, adding about 75,000 ounces to its output.

Another $70 million will be put towards the Suguiri mine, looking to add another 100,000 ounces to its production.

Shares in AngloGold Ashanti were up 0.35% to $88.22 apiece by mid-day Thursday in New York, valuing the company at $44.6 billion.

Profit on the rise

AngloGold reported a 12% increase for its EBITDA for Q3 2026 to $1,568 million, from $1,400 million for Q3 2025.

The company said on its Q3 earnings release that the growth is supported by the increase in the average gold price received per ounce to $4,239/oz, from $3,490/oz in the same period in 2025.

AngloGold Ashanti said its full year gold production guidance of 2,800,000 ounces to 3,170,000 ounces is reaffirmed.

Its gold production was about 3.65% more costly than the previous quarter, at $1,534 per ounce due gold royalties and higher fuel costs.

The company also reported that a worker died due to a rockfall at the Sukari underground mine in August 2026. Operations were suspended while investigations took place, but have since resumed.

(With files from Reuters)

item.title: MMG, Anglo American extend $500 million nickel deal deadline
item.description: The extension comes as European regulators continue to investigate the deal and its impact on steel production.
item.dc:creator: Marina Meireles
item.content:encoded:
MMG, Anglo American extend $500 million nickel deal deadline

Marina Meireles | November 3, 2026 | 10:43 am Regulatory Issues   Top Companies   Asia   Latin America   Nickel

Niquelândia processes both nickel and manganese from Codemin and Barro Alto sites. ( Image courtesy of Anglo American. )

MMG (HKEX: 1208) and Anglo American (LON: AAL) extended the deadline for their $500-million Brazilian nickel deal by two months as European Union regulators scrutinize its potential impact on the region’s stainless steel industry.

The companies agreed to move the long-stop date from Oct. 31 to Dec. 31, 2026, rather than terminate the transaction after failing to secure regulatory approval. The extension gives t

hem time to address concerns raised by the European Commission (EC), which has launched an in-depth Phase II investigation and is expected to issue its decision by Dec. 21.

MMG said it will continue to work with the EU and Anglo American to assist the EU in its review.

Anglo agreed last year to sell its Brazilian nickel operations to MMG, prompting regulatory scrutiny over the potential impact on ferronickel supplies. The deal includes two ferronickel and two greenfield projects in Brazil.

Brazil probes Anglo’s $500M nickel sale to China’s MMG

Twists and Turns

While the deal was announced in early 2025, the EU has been reviewing its possibility and the impacts it would have on ferronickel supply for the Union’s steel production since September 2025.

The European Commission (EC) is primarily concerned about whether the acquisition could allow MMG to divert Brazilian ferronickel away from Europe. This concern arises as the EU seeks to reduce its dependence on China for ferronickel and steel production.

Those that oppose the deal say that regulators need to consider how the acquisition would impact competition between major economies in a rather unstable geopolitical environment.

Anglo American and MMG argue that there’s plenty of ferronickel availability across the market, and Chinese control wouldn’t affect competition.

Amid the EU’s review, Anglo American said it would likely close its Brazilian nickel operation if the EU blocks MMG’s acquisition, Reuters reported.

Anglo American threatens to close Brazilian nickel operation if EU blocks sale to MMG

Ahead of the original long-stop date, MMG offered guarantees to maintain ferronickel supplies to European stainless steel producers aiming to ease the EU’s concerns.

The antitrust committee decision on the deal is expected to come out by the end of 2026, leaving the companies with about 10 days to decide how to move forward.
